ledger.claim: The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08(a) is discharged on the face of the record: the trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all carry the same trip identifier TRP-00113, and the gps_trace's first fix at 2026-08-05T18:47:10+08:00 coincides exactly with the trip_record's started_at, so the three artifacts describe one and the same trip and the same pickup event.

The gps_trace is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: it is one continuous run of 217 fixes at a 10-second sampling interval with coverage_pct 100, gaps an empty list and max_gap_sec 0.0, so none of limbs (a), (b) or (c) fires. The trace distance of 20.18 km is therefore a reliable, unbroken measurement of this trip, and this case does not escalate under POL-RD-10(3) for want of independent corroboration.

The rider is not a repeat deviation claimant and no heightened corroboration hurdle applies to her: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, both well below the POL-RD-08 triggers of 4 claims and 1 substantiated claim, so POL-RD-08 imposes no requirement of corroboration beyond the gps_trace on this claim.

Honest assessment, which the rider does not stretch: the claim in the dispute measures the trip against the solo optimal of 15.8 km, but POL-RD-12 fixes the POL-RD-01 baseline for a RYDE_POOL booking at the matched-itinerary optimal carried on the trip_record (optimal_distance_km 19.4 km, the Punggol -> Hougang co-rider pickup -> Raffles Place pool quoted at match time 18:42), leaving solo_optimal_distance_km as reference only. Measured against that correct baseline the gps_trace exceeds the optimal by 0.78 km, or 4.02% of optimal - neither greater than the 0.8 km absolute gate nor greater than 20% of optimal, so neither POL-RD-01 establishment test passes, no deviation is established on this trip's own evidence, and no POL-RD-02 recomputation refund arises. The rider does not ask for a remedy the policy's arithmetic cannot reach.

The rider's 15.8 km figure is trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km, which the policy carries for reference only. On a RYDE_POOL trip the POL-RD-01 baseline is the matched-itinerary optimal recorded in trip_record.optimal_distance_km, and that is 19.4 km — the platform's pooled quote for Punggol to the Hougang co-rider pickup and on to Raffles Place, as the trip_record's optimal_route_source states. A claim that measures excess against the solo optimal has cited the wrong field and fails on that ground alone.

The governing distance is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which POL-RD-01 makes the deciding field precisely because trip_record.actual_distance_km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test. The trace is 20.18 km against a matched-itinerary optimal of 19.4 km — an excess of 0.78 km and 4.02%. Both POL-RD-01 tests must pass. 0.78 km is not greater than the 0.8 km absolute threshold and 4.02% is not greater than the 20% percentage threshold, so no deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The result does not turn on which distance field is read. Even taking the trip_record's own rounded 20.2 km, the excess over the 19.4 km matched itinerary is 0.80 km — not GREATER than the 0.8 km absolute threshold POL-RD-01 requires, since that test is strict — and 4.1%, nowhere near the 20% percentage threshold. On either reading both establishment tests fail and no deviation exists however the rider characterises the trip.

The Hougang leg the rider complains about is a platform-matched co-rider pickup, not a driver detour. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting a co-rider on a platform-matched pooled itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied. The system chat message sent at 18:42:04, before the trip started at 18:47:10, reads 'Co-rider matched. Your pooled route now includes one pickup at Hougang Central before your drop-off. Estimated 19.4 km, 34 min' — the same 19.4 km the trip_record stores as the matched-itinerary optimal. The driver simply drove the route the app displayed to him.

The rider carries the initial burden under POL-RD-08 and must show an excess meeting the POL-RD-01 threshold, measured from an unimpaired gps_trace. The trace here is unimpaired: 100% coverage, 217 fixes, no gaps, a maximum gap of 0.0 seconds and a 10-second sampling interval against an expected 10 seconds. On that clean trace the excess is only 0.78 km. The burden is not discharged.

No repeat-deviation pattern can be established under POL-RD-06. driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 and driver_profile.completed_trips_90d is 471, so both the count test (3 or more) and the ratio test (0.05 or more, with at least 40 completed trips) fail. POL-RD-06 is not engaged, and in any event it can never be used to establish that this particular trip deviated.

I do not rely on traffic-closure exoneration, and I say why on the record: EV-ADVIS-00113-01 carries no payload and is a MISSING artifact at weight 0.0, so no advisory covers this corridor and POL-RD-03 cannot be run. That absence costs the driver nothing here, because the deviation fails POL-RD-01 on the threshold arithmetic alone and the driver needs no exculpatory clause to defeat it.

Because no deviation is established, POL-RD-02's optimal-route recomputation never runs and the charged fare stands as billed. POL-GEN-03 makes that outcome NO_ACTION, which on this rider-filed dispute leaves fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd at 0.0: the driver retains the SGD 26.83 legitimately billed for driving the matched pooled itinerary the platform assigned him.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider: I accept that you were charged SGD 26.83 and that your own Punggol-to-Raffles-Place route is about 15.8 km. But this was a RYDE_POOL booking. Under POL-RD-12, the baseline for a pooled trip is the platform’s matched pooled itinerary, stored on the trip_record as optimal_distance_km = 19.4 km, not the solo-rider figure solo_optimal_distance_km = 15.8 km, which is reference only. The app told you at 18:42:04, before the trip started, that a co-rider at Hougang had been matched and that the pooled route was estimated at 19.4 km. The Hougang leg is therefore the co-rider pickup, not an unexplained driver detour. The governing GPS trace distance is 20.18 km, an excess of 0.78 km over 19.4 km, or 4.02%. POL-RD-01 requires the excess to be both greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20%. It is neither. Even using the rounded trip_record distance of 20.2 km, the excess is exactly 0.80 km, which is still not greater than 0.8 km, and 4.1%, far below 20%. No deviation is established, so POL-RD-02’s recomputed-fare refund never runs. To the driver: your account is accepted. There is no billing-integrity correction under POL-RD-09(4): the fare_breakdown shows no ERP gantries, no airport surcharge, and no charge line without a counterpart in the trace or trip_record. No driver compensation is due under POL-RD-04 because the billed distance of 20.2 km is not less than the GPS trace distance of 20.18 km; the shortfall test is not met. The GPS trace is unimpaired for policy purposes (217 fixes, 100% coverage, no gaps, 10-second sampling), identifiers and timestamps match, and my confidence is 0.95, above the 0.70 floor, so no escalation applies. The charge stands as billed.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
